newsitem.title: USA: Boeing expects to complete MD merger Aug. 1.
newsitem.headline: Boeing expects to complete MD merger Aug. 1.

text.p: Boeing Co expects the European Union to approve its planned $14 billion merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp in time for the deal to close August 1, a Boeing spokeswoman said Tuesday.

Boeing filed a written statement with the European Commission Monday, outlining how the aerospace giant could address the three major areas of concern cited by European officials considering the merger, Boeing spokeswoman Sherry Nebel said.
She declined to comment on details of Boeing's proposal to the European Union, but said the company was confident it would result in approval of the merger deal by the EU's July 30 deadline.
Shareholders of both Boeing and McDonnell Douglas are scheduled to meet July 25 to vote on ratifying the merger, which was approved Tuesday by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission.
Nebel said the merged entity would start operations officially as of August 4, a Monday.
In a statement, Boeing Chairman and Chief Executive Phil Condit said the company was "deeply gratified" by the FTC approval.

"The FTC review was one of the most detailed and extensive in the history of proposed mergers," Condit said. "Boeing and McDonnell Douglas together presented the agency with more than 5 million pages of documents, numerous issue papers and testimony by experts from both companies an other parties."
Harry Stonecipher, president and chief executive of McDonnell Douglas, said, "We are delighted with the FTC decision and look forward to bringing these two companies together."
